description: Cosmic Siblings is a sibling team from Malaysia exploring how NASA Earth imagery can become sound. We are taking on The Earth Information Jukebox to make Earth science engaging and accessible through sonification.
summary: Remix Earth lets people explore NASA Earth imagery through music. Users select an ocean or aerosol region, and a moving scan turns its changing colors into musical notes. They can adjust the instruments, mix different regions, or create a melody. A separate atmosphere model uses temperature and wind data to show how sound could curve through the air. An animated pulse connects the starting point to a possible arrival point, with an optional delayed sound. By combining images, music, and animation, our project gives beginners a playful way to explore Earth patterns and atmospheric science.
details:
Remix Earth was created to make Earth imagery more approachable for beginners. Instead of only looking at a map, users can choose a region and hear its changing colors.

A moving scan reads different colors across the selected region and turns them into notes. As the NASA video changes, the sound changes too. Users can choose an instrument and adjust bass, treble, smoothness, and other Sound Lab controls.

Selected regions become music nodes. They can play individually, one after another, or together. Users can also build a melody by choosing notes and assigning each step to a region. In this mode, the chosen notes control the melody while the region's colors shape the sound.

Animated surfaces help users see differences within each region. Brighter pixels appear higher, making visual patterns easier to compare. These surfaces represent image brightness, not actual mountains or terrain.

The atmosphere feature explores where sound could travel after it starts. Using NASA MERRA-2 temperature and wind data, the app calculates a simplified sound path for the selected area. Users change its direction and starting angle. Point A shows where the sound starts. Point B shows where a returning path reaches its starting height elsewhere.

When Echo is enabled, a delayed copy plays as the animated pulse reaches B. The calculated travel time is divided by 1,000 for listening. This represents arrival at another location, rather than a reflection back to A. The model uses a single regional atmosphere profile and does not account for terrain, absorption, Earth curvature, or horizontal weather changes.

The project combines ocean imagery from 25 March 2007 to 3 March 2008, aerosol imagery from 1 August to 14 September 2024, and a separate atmosphere sample from 1 January 2025. They represent different periods. The sounds are created from image colors, and the atmosphere feature is an educational model.

The browser interface uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Web Audio API. A Python backend calculates the atmospheric sound paths. The app is hosted on Render, with source code available on GitHub.

Our aim is to encourage curiosity by letting users see, hear, and experiment with NASA imagery in one place.
